title: Shop item detail
one_line: Big rotating render on a plinth, rarity, what it changes, BUY or EQUIP.
opens: paywall-offer (if it is part of a bundle)

anatomy.spec: Standard NX Card, 380 wide, rarity-coloured rim accent, Lucky Six corners.
The item render, large, centred, slowly rotating (a die tumbles gently; a token turns) - rarity glow behind it, rays for legendary.
Item name, straddling the top edge.
Section label in the rarity colour: COMMON / RARE / EPIC / LEGENDARY.
One line, Nunito 14: what it changes. 'Your dice in every match.'
BUY (go green, localised price) or EQUIP (option amber) or OWNED-EQUIPPED (no button, outline only), straddling the bottom edge in a collar.

states: Locked - disabled price, unlock rule shown
Purchasing - spinner in the button, width unchanged
Purchase failed - a toast with the store's error, button returns to BUY
motion: Plinth idle rotation: slow, continuous, the only idle on the card.
Purchase success: a brief sparkle burst on the plinth, then the button becomes EQUIP.
data: RevenueCat package for price and purchase.
Ownership from the server after T-A3.
do_not: Do not skip the purchase-failed state.
Do not use a rarity colour anywhere but the rim accent, the label and the ribbon/glow - never as a button colour.
acceptance: Every state in 'states' is reachable and captured.
Price is the RevenueCat localised string.
Purchasing shows a spinner in the button; failure shows a toast and reverts cleanly.
steps: 2. Build the card with the rotating plinth and rarity glow.
3. Wire BUY to the RevenueCat package, with loading and failure states.
4. Wire EQUIP and the owned/equipped/locked states.
prompt:
Build the Ludo NX shop item detail popup.

Read SCREEN_PLANS/specs/SHARED_RULES.md, UI_BIBLE/LUDO_NX_UI_BIBLE.md sections 5.16 and 4.3, UI_BIBLE/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md section 7.1, and this whole file. Use only values from UI_BIBLE/tokens.json.

Standard NX Card popup: the item slowly rotating on a plinth with its rarity glow behind it, the item name as the nameplate, a rarity label, one line of what it changes, and BUY / EQUIP / OWNED-EQUIPPED / locked as the four states of the bottom-edge action button.

The price must come from the RevenueCat package as the store's localised string - never hard-coded. Build the purchasing state (spinner in the button) and the purchase-failed state (a toast, then revert to BUY) - both are usually skipped and both will happen to real players.

Follow the 'steps' array. Finish with bible section 11 and the 'acceptance' list.
